# Awesome Open-Source AI Cheat Sheets

![Awesome Open-Source AI Cheat Sheets: Build, Evaluate, Secure, Operate](assets/social-preview.png)

[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge-flat.svg)](https://awesome.re)
[![Validate collection](https://github.com/sraodev/awesome-opensource-ai-cheat-sheets/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sraodev/awesome-opensource-ai-cheat-sheets/actions/workflows/validate.yml)
[![2027 readiness](https://img.shields.io/badge/readiness-2027-8250df)](READINESS_2027.md)
[![Cheat sheets](https://img.shields.io/badge/cheat_sheets-10-238636)](#cheat-sheets)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

Practical, source-backed references for building, evaluating, securing, and operating open-source AI systems and software, plus honestly labeled open-weight or source-available models. The collection favors durable engineering decisions over model rankings and giant tool directories.

> **No link dump. No vendor ranking. No mislabeled “open” models.** Each sheet turns primary sources into a decision, an evidence record, and a release gate.

> [!NOTE]
> Links and time-sensitive claims were reviewed on **2026-08-24**. The [2027 readiness guide](READINESS_2027.md) is an engineering checklist based on current evidence, not a prediction of future products or laws.

This project uses the [Open Source AI Definition 1.0](https://opensource.org/ai/open-source-ai-definition) when calling an AI system open source. Public weights alone are labeled **open weights**, not open-source AI; incomplete evidence is labeled **openness unverified**. These are catalog assessments, not OSI certifications or legal opinions.

## Start here

- [2027 readiness checklist](READINESS_2027.md) — the evidence to assemble before calling an AI system production-ready.
- [Cheat-sheet index](#cheat-sheets) — choose the reference that matches the current engineering decision.

## What's new

- **2026-08-25:** Added an [evidence-based openness classification](#openness-and-supply-chain) using OSAID 1.0, SPDX 3.0.1, and model-signing guidance.
- **2026-08-25:** Added training and model adaptation gates for data, SFT, PEFT, preference optimization, distillation, and release to the [cheat-sheet index](#cheat-sheets).
- **2026-08-25:** Added a share-ready project identity, weekly validation, [security reporting](SECURITY.md), and [contribution standards](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## The short version

1. Define the task, output contract, risk tolerance, latency, and cost budget.
2. Establish a non-AI baseline and a representative evaluation set.
3. Start with a prompt and schema; add retrieval, tools, or autonomy only when the evals justify them.
4. Treat model output, retrieved content, tool metadata, and memory as untrusted data.
5. Give every tool the least privilege possible; require approval for consequential actions.
6. Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, approvals, failures, cost, and final outcomes without leaking sensitive content.
7. Gate releases on quality, safety, security, and operational thresholds; keep a tested rollback path.
8. Version prompts, schemas, models, data, tools, policies, and evals together.

## Cheat sheets

| Sheet | Use it when | Main deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| [AI system design](cheatsheets/ai-system-design.md) | Choosing between rules, prompting, retrieval, workflows, agents, or fine-tuning | A testable system contract and minimum architecture |
| [Open-source AI](cheatsheets/open-source-ai.md) | Determining what can actually be used, studied, modified, shared, and reproduced | An artifact, license, provenance, and supply-chain record |
| [Models and inference](cheatsheets/models-and-inference.md) | Selecting a model, license, runtime, precision, or serving shape | A workload-specific model and deployment decision record |
| [Training and model adaptation](cheatsheets/training-and-model-adaptation.md) | Changing model behavior after simpler approaches fail their evals | A reproducible training contract, adapted artifact, and release comparison |
| [Prompting and structured output](cheatsheets/prompting-and-structured-output.md) | Turning natural-language behavior into a stable interface | A prompt, schema, validation loop, and prompt eval |
| [Retrieval and context](cheatsheets/retrieval-and-context.md) | Answers depend on private, current, or source-citable knowledge | A permission-aware retrieval pipeline and retrieval eval |
| [Agents and MCP](cheatsheets/agents-and-mcp.md) | A model must select tools or adapt a plan across steps | Explicit tool contracts, approval gates, and protocol boundaries |
| [Multimodal systems](cheatsheets/multimodal-systems.md) | Handling images, audio, video, documents, or mixed-modality tasks | Typed media contracts and modality-specific evals and controls |
| [Evals and observability](cheatsheets/evals-and-observability.md) | Comparing changes or operating an AI feature in production | Versioned eval cases, release thresholds, and traces |
| [Security and governance](cheatsheets/security-and-governance.md) | The system handles sensitive data, external content, or actions | Threat model, control evidence, inventory, and incident plan |

Missing a primary source or spotted a stale claim? Open a [resource or correction request](https://github.com/sraodev/awesome-opensource-ai-cheat-sheets/issues/new?template=resource.yml) or follow the focused [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Curated primary references

These are standards, public guidance, and project-owned documentation used by the sheets.

### Interfaces and documentation

| Resource | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| [Model Context Protocol specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28) | Versioned interoperability for context, tools, and AI applications. |
| [A2A Protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/) | Open interoperability between opaque agentic applications. |
| [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/learn/getting-started-step-by-step) | Portable, machine-checkable output and tool-input contracts. |
| [Hugging Face Transformers](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers) | Open model architectures and inference tooling across text, vision, audio, video, and multimodal models. |
| [Hugging Face model cards](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards) | Intended use, limitations, training information, and evaluation results. |
| [Hugging Face dataset cards](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/datasets-cards) | Dataset contents, provenance, license, limitations, and responsible use. |

### Openness and supply chain

| Resource | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| [Open Source AI Definition 1.0](https://opensource.org/ai/open-source-ai-definition) | Defines the freedoms and preferred form for modifying an open-source AI system. |
| [SPDX 3.0.1 AI Profile](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/model/AI/AI/) | Standardized metadata for AI systems, models, datasets, and their declared and concluded licenses. |
| [OpenSSF Model Signing](https://openssf.org/projects/model-signing/) | Signing and verification for model artifacts across the ML supply chain. |

### Evaluation and operations

| Resource | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| [NIST AI Resource Center](https://airc.nist.gov/) | Operational resources for AI risk management and testing, evaluation, verification, and validation. |
| [Language Model Evaluation Harness](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) | Reproducible evaluation tasks across model backends. |
| [Inspect AI](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai) | Open-source framework for model and agent evaluations. |
| [promptfoo](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo) | Test matrices, assertions, and red-team workflows for prompts and applications. |
| [OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai) | Shared traces, metrics, and events for model clients, agents, and MCP. |
| [Langfuse](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse) | Open-source tracing, prompt management, and evaluation. |
| [Arize Phoenix](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix) | Open-source AI observability and evaluation. |

### Security and assurance

| Resource | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| [OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026](https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/) | Prioritized risks for autonomous and tool-using systems. |
| [OWASP AI Security Verification Standard](https://owasp.org/www-project-artificial-intelligence-security-verification-standard-aisvs-docs/) | Testable requirements across the AI system lifecycle. |
| [NSA MCP security considerations](https://www.nsa.gov/Press-Room/Press-Releases-Statements/Press-Release-View/Article/4496698/nsa-releases-security-design-considerations-for-ai-driven-automation-leveraging/) | Deployment guidance for AI-driven automation using MCP. |
| [PyRIT](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT) | Open-source risk identification and red-team automation for generative AI. |

### Open-source building blocks

| Area | Starting points |
|---|---|
| Local and hosted inference | [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp), [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) |
| Retrieval and knowledge | [Haystack](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack), [RAGFlow](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow), [pgvector](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) |
| Agent applications | [LangGraph](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph), [Pydantic AI](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai) |

Projects here are starting points, not endorsements. Benchmark them on your own data, constraints, and threat model.

- [Awesome Generative AI](https://github.com/filipecalegario/awesome-generative-ai) — a large directory of tools, models, and research.
- [AI Engineering Cheatsheets](https://github.com/louisfb01/ai-engineering-cheatsheets) — decision tables and playbooks for AI engineering.
- [Awesome AI Cheatsheets](https://github.com/ShowMeAI-Hub/awesome-AI-cheatsheets) — classic ML, data-science, and library references in Chinese.

## How entries are selected

A resource should be:

- directly useful for building, evaluating, securing, or operating AI systems;
- maintained by its project, standards body, government publisher, or a credible open community;
- concise enough to support a quick decision or next action;
- publicly accessible without an account;
- honestly labeled as open-source AI, open-source software, open weights, or source available based on the published artifacts and terms;
- clear about its source and license when local redistribution is proposed;
- current, or explicitly versioned and labeled as historical;
- free of affiliate links and unnecessary tracking parameters.

If these checklists save you time, star the repository so you can find them again and share the specific sheet that helped your team.

## Validation

Run the repository-owned deterministic checks:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_collection.py
```

GitHub Actions also checks external links on pull requests, changes to `main`, and a weekly schedule.
